subject: Recap & next steps — inference TCO (batching/caching) for Cargofy
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Mendez <alicia@cargofy.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cargofy.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Recap & next steps — inference TCO (batching/caching) for Cargofy

Hi Alicia / Tom,

Thanks again for the 45 min call — really appreciated the transparency on where Cargofy is trying to get with automated invoice ingestion and downstream entity normalization. Quick recap from our side and next steps so we keep momentum.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Token spend volatility: spikes during month-end batching cause budget overruns.
- Latency requirements: 95th pct <= 350ms for user-facing validation flows.
- Ops overhead: internal infra experiments have eaten engineering cycles and not hit predictable TCO.

Stated goals / success metrics:
- Proof-of-value pilot that reduces per-transaction inference cost by >= 40% vs current managed LLM run rate.
- Monthly predictable spend within a $28k–$40k budget band for the pilot (you mentioned a soft cap).
- Deployment into your VPC or our Dedicated pool depending on security sign-off.

Preliminary economics (very high level):
- Baseline (current): ~0.85–1.2 USD per 1k tokens at your observed prompt sizes (including retries).
- Optimized pilot (batching + prefix caching + a quantized model): target ~0.35–0.55 USD per 1k tokens depending on batch shape and hit rates.
- Primary levers: request batching, prefix/KV caching for repeated invoice templates, and opting into a quantized 4-bit model variant for non-chat prompts.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the internal budget band you want us to design the pilot around (you mentioned ~$30k/mo as a preferred target)?
2) Please share a sample of typical token distributions (anonymized) if possible — a short CSV or example payload helps us size batching impact.
3) I'll loop in Marissa (SE) and Priyom (solutions analyst) to produce a 2-week pilot blueprint with explicit ROI scenarios and a sample batching profile.

I attached a short outline (will send full TCO blueprint after we get the token sample). If it helps, we can also ship a 2-week free pilot credit to accelerate the decision.

Thanks — speaking tomorrow at 10am PT? If not, tell me a time that works.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: outline_onepager.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: Alicia Mendez <alicia@cargofy.com>

Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — inference TCO (batching/caching) for Cargofy

Sean — thanks for the clear summary. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Budget: our procurement team has signaled a hard pilot ceiling at $32k/month unless we see clear committed savings in month 1 that justify an uplift.
- Token sample: attaching a redacted sample of 500 requests (token_counts.csv) — includes prompt, expected output length, and frequency.
- Timeline: we want the pilot to start in July; decision on expanding to production by mid-August.

Can you include in the ROI scenarios an explicit line-item for engineering time saved (we've got a rough internal estimate of 40 engineer-hours/month tied to managing model variants and retry logic)? That factor moves us.

Also, curious about how Redwood handles graceful degradation in the event a quantized variant diverges on rare edge-cases — do you have a fallback / canary plan?

Appreciate you moving fast on this.

— Alicia
Alicia Mendez
Head of ML Products | Cargofy

Can you do the following?
- Priyom: run a quick sizing run on the attached CSV to produce 3 ROI scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive). Include per-1k-token cost with and without batching + prefix cache and an engineering-time dollarized line-item.

Please include sample batching profile (CSV) and callouts for any SOW or credit we should propose. Alicia asked about a 2-week credit — what's reasonable to offer without approval?

Thanks — Sean

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap & next steps — inference TCO (batching/caching) for Cargofy

Adding the plan here — high level before I produce the full 2-week blueprint and CSVs.

Summary of approach:
- Model profile: start with a quantized LLaMA-family 13B variant for parsing steps (non-chat), keep chat/dialog if any on full-precision small chat model.
- Batching: target batching for high-frequency templates — expected batch sizes 6–10 for the mid-month spike window, 1–2 for steady-state.
- Prefix/KV caching: implement template-level KV cache for the 12 most common invoice schemas (hoping for 35–48% cache hit rate from the token sample).
- Fallback/canary: run 5% traffic on FP model + strict divergence monitor (BLEU/embedding-sim threshold) — automatic fallback to FP on anomaly + alert to Cargofy via webhook.

Preliminary ROI (ballpark; Priyom will produce precise numbers):
- Conservative: $0.60 / 1k tokens (optimized) vs $1.05 baseline => ~43% cost reduction.
- Expected: $0.47 / 1k tokens => ~55% reduction.
- Aggressive: $0.33 / 1k tokens => ~68% reduction (requires higher cache hit-rate ~55% and bigger batch tail).

Engineering-time savings: we model 40 hours/month at a $150/hr fully loaded rate => $6k/month in recoverable ops cost for the pilot. Include this line in all scenarios.

Pilot offer and credits:
- We can offer a $5k pilot credit on the Hosted plan without additional approvals. Anything larger or a multi-week Dedicated commit credit needs sales-lead approval.

Deliverables next 48h:
- sample_batching_profile.csv (expected batch shapes by hour)
- detailed ROI spreadsheet (3 scenarios)
- 2-week pilot blueprint (infra choices + canary + monitoring hooks)

I'll assemble and attach the blueprint and CSV.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — talk soon.
